research_scope: Source-free whole-formulation-anchored review of shared prerequisite identities; no source/definition mutation, no parent-definition equivalence, no freeze or gate change.

aliases.reason: The representable-presheaf statement sets h_U(X)=Hom_C(X,U) for a category with set-valued hom-collections; the preadditive-category statement supplies abelian-group structures on Hom_C(X,Y). Their common prerequisite is a hom-set of arrows with specified domain/codomain; preadditive structure and contravariant precomposition are distinct parent conditions.

The linear-kernel source explicitly identifies ker T with T^{-1}({0_W}). This is the inverse image of a singleton under an arbitrary function, already covered by the canonical general preimage f^{-1}[B]; linearity and use of the zero vector specify the parent kernel statement, not a new inverse-image operation.

The preadditive cokernel requires p∘f=0 and the preadditive kernel requires f∘i=0, each zero being the additive identity in the appropriate Hom abelian group. They share the typed zero-morphism construction, even though the arrow compositions and respective universal properties are different parent conditions.

The uniformizer source tests whether (π) equals a discrete valuation ring's maximal ideal, while the principal-ideal-domain and prime-element sources use an ideal generated by one element. In all cases (a)={ra:r∈R} is the shared principal-ideal prerequisite; maximality, primality and DVR hypotheses stay in their original formulations.
